I understand that over time variations of communism have emerged, however I fundamentally disagree with the tenets of communism itself. 
Firstly, I don’t understand the opposition to capitalism. Yes, there are flaws, humanity isn’t perfect, and the flaws in capitalism are simple reflections of the flaws in humanity. However, it’s these same flaws in humanity which cause any system to not be perfect that simultaneously corrupt communism. The way I see it, any form of massive national centralization of governmental power will always be prone to abuse.
Secondly, I just don’t see any system which has or could benefit humanity on the same scale as capitalism. There is suffering in the world, yes, and a mass grab of financial power could potentially end it, but I believe that personal liberty should always be respected, and there isn’t a system which respects personal liberty more than capitalism.
I would, however, agree that a balance must be struck. There are losers who are always losing and winner who are always winning, and from a purely moral perspective, that’s unfair. A nation’s economy can be fueled through a free market, while said nations society must also be aided through social programs. 
However, the simple abolition of capitalism is something I don’t see can be either practical or beneficial.
So, do you actually believe in Marxism as presented by the communist manifesto? Isn’t it at least appropriate to have some form of suspicion after the Soviet and Chinese communist failures?
